text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- An editorial says that anti-Berisha feeling in south Albania shows his Democratic Party will be overwhelmingly defeated in the June 29 elections.
- More than 6,000 Albanians are drug addicts, paper says.
- Democratic Party senior member Azem Hajdari called on Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to disband so-called committees of public salvation in south Albania.
- Greek consulate in southernmost town of Gjirokaster decided to stop issuing visas due to lawlessness and violence.
- Greek soldiers, part of Alba multinational force, shot and killed an Albanian man in a fight after he tried to sell them drugs.
- Government issued a draft decree on transparency of pyramid investment schemes which should be signed by President Sali Berisha.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The United Nations Security Council has voted to extend the mandate of a multinational protection force in Albania till August.
- The Democratic Party has accused the Socialist Party of organising bandits and former security officers in order to shrink the electoral geography of the Democrats.

- The national unity government has approved a draft law for the auditing of collapsed pyramid schemes but, contrary to the expectations of the President Sali Berisha, it has not charged the Finance Minister with carrying it out.
- Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano said the party would opt for cohabitation with the opposition if they came to power after the June 29 elections.
ALBANIA

- Romanian soldiers serving in the international force in the southern Albanian town of Gjirokaster have, in two separate incidents, rescued a team of OSCE election observers and prevented an attack on an aid convoy.
- Democratic Party branches in south have been threatened by leftist extremists saying they must not hold electoral rallies.
- European Union agreed with OCSE that early elections should be held on June 29.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE

- The Democratic Party has accused its rival Socialists of launching a campaign of terror against Democrats in the districts, and charged the Socialists with wanting to fill the new parliament with criminals.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano told a crowd of supporters that the Socialists were prepared to rule in coalition with other leftist and centrist parties after elections.
- All Albanians are united from south to north, this is Socialist Party electoral message.
